rows.my_view: CVNA is very overvalued at $70, even after the 28% pullback from its high.
rows.committee: We agree it's expensive: ~35x GAAP earnings and a 1% FCF yield price durable growth, structural margins, and open credit markets all at once, and even the cheaper 25.7x read is rich for a cyclical dealer.

rows.my_view: Not addressed directly beyond the overvaluation call.
rows.committee: Revenue reaccelerated +52% in Q1, but the five-year line is a V-shape that fell to $10.77B in FY23, so runway exists while durability is unproven and units-sold data is missing.
The gross margin climb from 7% to 21% may be a used-car pricing cycle rather than a moat, and a 3-4 point give-back would roughly halve a 9% operating margin.

rows.my_view: Implied weak as part of the overvaluation view.
rows.committee: We agree the moat is narrow: a real but cyclical scale edge in reconditioning and logistics, with no network effect, no switching cost, and a weak brand that must buy demand through advertising.
Shares expanded ~70% in one year (661M to 1.12B FY24-FY25), quietly diluting the recovery story, with the cause undisclosed in the materials.
The deeper risk is that the margin recovery is cyclical (GPU roll-over) and that profit leans on selling loans, so earnings could crater on a credit wobble even if cars keep selling.

rows.my_view: None stated; the owner has no falsification trigger and treats the 28% pullback as partial validation.
rows.committee: You are treating a pullback from a 1,095% three-year run as evidence of fair value and owning a conclusion with no kill-switch, which risks a pass you regret if July 29 GPU proves structural.
Gross profit per unit direction against Manheim used-car prices on the July 29 print is the single number that settles whether the margin is structural or a cycle.

confidence.label: Moderate
confidence.why: The valuation and moat calls are strongly supported, but the metrics that decide the thesis — GPU, units, finance mix, and real debt — are entirely absent from the materials.

final_verdict: Overvalued instinct is right, but it needs a written kill-switch, not permanent avoidance — Watchlist until July 29 GPU decides it.
